skill.name: skill-developer
skill.description: Guide for creating, testing, and troubleshooting Claude Code skills. It covers SKILL.md structure, skill-rules.json triggers, hook behavior, enforcement levels, skip conditions, and progressive disclosure.
skill.summary: Build Claude Code skills with triggers, hooks, and validation guidance.
skill.author: diet103

security_audit.summary: All static detections appear to be false positives from Markdown examples, inline code, or Claude Code configuration paths. No evidence found for prompt injection, credential access, network exfiltration, hidden execution, or system reconnaissance intent. The skill includes optional local test commands, so users should review commands before running them.

remediation.issue: Shell examples can execute local hook files when copied by a user.
remediation.suggestion: Label command examples as optional local tests and advise users to run them only in trusted repositories.

remediation.issue: Skip markers and environment overrides can weaken project guardrails.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance that skips should be temporary or tied to a documented review decision.

content.value_statement: Building skills can be error-prone when triggers, hooks, and rules are spread across files. This skill gives structured guidance for creating, testing, and troubleshooting Claude Code skills.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to create a SKILL.md file with required frontmatter.
Shows how to configure keyword, intent, file path, and content triggers.
Describes UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, and Stop hook behavior.
Provides local test commands for checking skill activation behavior.
Documents skip conditions, session tracking, and enforcement levels.
Uses reference files to keep core skill guidance under the 500-line limit.
limitations: It is documentation only and does not create files automatically.
Examples assume a Claude Code project with the expected hook files.
It does not validate rule files without running local tools.
It does not replace security review for custom hook scripts.

use_cases.title: Create a new project skill
use_cases.description: Plan the skill name, frontmatter, trigger rules, and test cases before adding it to a Claude Code project.

use_cases.title: Standardize team guardrails
use_cases.description: Document when a skill should suggest guidance, warn users, or block risky edits with a hook.

use_cases.title: Debug activation problems
use_cases.description: Trace missing suggestions, broad matches, invalid rule files, and hook registration issues.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a Claude Code skill for my topic. Include the name, description, trigger keywords, and a simple test plan.

prompt_templates.title: Tune Skill Triggers
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these skill triggers for false positives and missed matches. Suggest safer keywords, intent patterns, and file path patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Activation
prompt_templates.scenario: Troubleshoot a skill that does not appear
prompt_templates.prompt: A Claude Code skill is not activating. Walk through rule syntax, hook registration, test commands, and likely configuration mistakes.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Guardrail Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a guardrail skill for a risky workflow. Define when to block, when to suggest, skip conditions, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Create a skill for database migration guidance.
output: A concise skill purpose and frontmatter description.
Trigger keywords and intent patterns for migration work.
A focused test checklist for activation and false positives.

output_examples.input: Troubleshoot a skill that does not trigger for frontend prompts.
output: Likely keyword and intent pattern gaps.
Hook registration checks and local test guidance.

output_examples.input: Review a proposed guardrail skill for edit blocking.
output: A recommendation for block, suggest, or warn enforcement.
Skip condition guidance for reviewed exceptions.
Testing criteria for safety, clarity, and developer friction.

best_practices: Keep SKILL.md focused and move detailed references into one level of supporting files.
Test each trigger with realistic prompts, file paths, and negative examples.
Use blocking guardrails only for clear correctness or safety risks.
anti_patterns: Using broad keywords that activate skills for unrelated work.
Adding complex hook behavior without a clear test plan.
Leaving permanent skip markers in files without documented review.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you design Claude Code skills, configure activation rules, and troubleshoot hook behavior.

faq.question: Does it generate a complete skill automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides templates, examples, and review guidance that you apply in your project.

faq.question: Which trigger types does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers keyword triggers, intent patterns, file path patterns, and content patterns.

faq.question: Can it help with guardrail skills?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains block, suggest, and warn enforcement, including when each level is appropriate.

faq.question: Does it require local command execution?
faq.answer: Some troubleshooting steps use optional local test commands. Review commands before running them.

faq.question: Is this useful for Codex users?
faq.answer: Yes. Codex users can use the guidance to review skill structure, marketplace readiness, and trigger quality.
